k1p1-2.name: text#2
k1p1-2.text: KP04 Unlabeled data can still reveal structure

k1p1-41.name: text#41
k1p1-41.text: No answers to check against, but we still must define “similar”

k1p2-2.name: text#2
k1p2-2.text: Clustering gives group numbers, not class names

k1p2-25.name: text#25
k1p2-25.text: group numbers are not ground-truth names

k1p2-27.name: text#27
k1p2-27.text: Still to decide: the similarity, the cluster count, the scoring

k1p3-2.name: text#2
k1p3-2.text: The same 15 points can form piles at different granularity

k1p3-36.name: text#36
k1p3-36.text:
9 points close on the left,
6 close on the right.

But how many piles,
and how finely to split?

A criterion decides.

k1p3-38.name: text#38
k1p3-38.text: Same coordinates, only the granularity changes

k1p4-2.name: text#2
k1p4-2.text: k-means alternates two steps: assign, update

k1p4-5.name: text#5
k1p4-5.text: 1. Assign: each point to its nearest center

k1p4-32.name: text#32
k1p4-32.text: 2. Update: move each center to its points' mean

k1p4-65.name: text#65
k1p4-65.text: Repeat until assignments stop changing: an algorithm, not a lookup

k1p5-2.name: text#2
k1p5-2.text: Different cluster counts split the same points differently

k1p5-100.name: text#100
k1p5-100.text: More clusters need not be nested: initialization and local solutions matter

k1p6-2.name: text#2
k1p6-2.text: Distances come from the specified centers

k1p6-64.name: text#64
k1p6-64.text: (6, 6) is center B: its distance is exactly 0, so the source's 1.4 cannot hold

k1p6-66.name: text#66
k1p6-66.text: Keep centers and points, recompute; never change centers to fit a wrong table

k1p7-49.name: text#49
k1p7-49.text:
a prescribed
feature selection,
not PCA, not learned

k1p7-51.name: text#51
k1p7-51.text: The low-dimensional representation is an embedding; a criterion decides what stays

k1p8-40.name: text#40
k1p8-40.text: Different inputs, same output: the second coordinate's difference is lost; all 15 samples remain, in 10 positions

k1p8-42.name: text#42
k1p8-42.text: Collisions do not delete 5 samples; they make them indistinguishable

k1p9-2.name: text#2
k1p9-2.text: Even without labels, say what to preserve

k1p9-23.name: text#23
k1p9-23.text:
Unsupervised reduction uses inputs only; supervised reduction can use class labels or other side information.
Fisher discriminant analysis uses labels, unlike the unlabeled setting.

k1p9-25.name: text#25
k1p9-25.text: Next, KP05: what structure can extra feedback help preserve? $\to$

steps.label: KP04 Unlabeled data can still reveal structure
Unlabeled data and clustering · 1/9
steps.speakerNotes: KP03 ended by removing the labels. This unit asks what we can do with inputs only. First, clustering. (The fruit is an analogy, not the note's data.)

steps.label: Unlabeled data and clustering · 1/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: A pile of unnamed fruit.

steps.label: Unlabeled data and clustering · 1/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Grouping them by appearance is clustering.

steps.label: Unlabeled data and clustering · 1/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The source's 5 apples and 5 cucumbers illustrate withholding category names, not removing all assumptions. Similarity and the number of groups must still be specified.

steps.label: Group numbers are not names · 2/9
steps.speakerNotes: Unsupervised learning does not use target classes for training. Clustering resembles classification in form: a d-dimensional input maps to one of m group identifiers.

steps.label: Group numbers are not names · 2/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: In classification the names are supplied; training has correct names to compare.

steps.label: Group numbers are not names · 2/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Clustering has only identifiers, not supplied ground-truth names.

steps.label: Group numbers are not names · 2/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: So we must still decide how to measure similarity, how many groups, and how to accept a result.

steps.label: The 15 teaching points · 3/9
steps.speakerNotes: Look at the source's 15 unitless teaching points. They are not measurements with known true classes.

steps.label: The 15 teaching points · 3/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: By eye, one cluster on the left and one on the right.

steps.label: The 15 teaching points · 3/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Whether to split further has no single answer; a criterion decides.

steps.label: The 15 teaching points · 3/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The coordinates stay fixed; only the cluster count changes.

steps.label: Two steps of k-means · 4/9
steps.speakerNotes: The source uses k-means. Assignment gives each point to its nearest center; update moves each center to the mean of its points. This page uses m equal to 2 and the source's fixed initial centers.

steps.label: Two steps of k-means · 4/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Assignment: blue points are closer to the left initial center, orange to the right.

steps.label: Two steps of k-means · 4/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Update: each center moves to the mean of its points, about 3.83 and 11.83.

steps.label: Two steps of k-means · 4/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Repeat until assignments stop changing. Centers are marked with crosses, not interpreted as true fruit categories.

steps.label: Different cluster counts · 5/9
steps.speakerNotes: m equal to 2: with the fixed initial centers, the groups end with 9 and 6 points.

steps.label: Different cluster counts · 5/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: m equal to 3: the groups have 3, 6 and 6 points. The source narrative mentions 1 and 6 left-side points, inconsistent with its 15-point code; recomputing from the original coordinates and seeds gives 3, 6, 6.

steps.label: Different cluster counts · 5/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: m equal to 5: 3 points per group. Axes are identical; group identifiers do not mean the same category across panels.

steps.label: Different cluster counts · 5/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: This example admits finer groups, but arbitrary k-means solutions need not be nested as m grows; initialization and local solutions matter.

steps.label: Recompute distances · 6/9
steps.speakerNotes: The guide's 5-point example: the specified centers are A at (1,1) and B at (6,6), but the source table lists inconsistent distances. We keep centers and points and recompute Euclidean distances.

steps.label: Recompute distances · 6/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Each point connects to its nearest center: blue dashed lines to A, orange to B.

steps.label: Recompute distances · 6/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Step by step: the first point to B is the square root of 25 plus 25, which is the square root of 50, about 7.0711. Check (6,6): it is center B, so its distance to B must be 0, and the source's 1.4 cannot hold. These 5 points get one assignment, unlike the converged 15-point example.

steps.label: Recompute distances · 6/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: All distances were recomputed by program.

steps.label: Reduction and embedding · 7/9
steps.speakerNotes: Clustering keeps the coordinates and adds group identifiers; dimensionality reduction maps d-dimensional data to a p-dimensional embedding with p less than d.

steps.label: Reduction and embedding · 7/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: This page is a supplement: the simplest prescribed projection on the same 15 points.

steps.label: Reduction and embedding · 7/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Each point drops straight down onto the horizontal axis, keeping only the first coordinate.

steps.label: Reduction and embedding · 7/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: This is dimensionality reduction by feature selection, not PCA and not a learned projection. The criterion decides which changes are kept.

steps.label: Information loss · 8/9
steps.speakerNotes: After keeping the first coordinate, the 15 points sit on one line.

steps.label: Information loss · 8/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: The 5 orange positions each hold two samples, marked times 2; the other 5 hold one each. The vertical stacking encodes no feature; it only shows the overlap.

steps.label: Information loss · 8/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: For example (1,2) and (1,3) both become 1: the second-coordinate difference is lost. All 15 samples remain, in 10 positions; collisions do not delete 5 samples.

steps.label: Information loss · 8/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: All positions and counts were computed by program.

steps.label: Criteria without labels · 9/9
steps.speakerNotes: Without target labels, assumptions and scoring criteria are still necessary.

steps.label: Criteria without labels · 9/9 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: First, similarity: how is distance measured?

steps.label: Criteria without labels · 9/9 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Second, the cluster count; for reduction, say what to preserve.

steps.label: Criteria without labels · 9/9 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Unsupervised reduction uses inputs; supervised reduction can use labels or side information. The next unit asks what structure extra feedback helps preserve. The note's practice questions stay in the note.
